text:
Justin Barron had nine points in 52 games for Nashville last season, without a goal. Now with St. Louis, his fourth NHL team at 25, he has 15 points in 22 games, and his ice time has climbed from about 14 minutes to nearly 17. It's the clearest breakout on the Blues' blue line, and the coverage has noticed: The Hockey Writers and Yardbarker both ran pieces on how it's finally clicking, and Hockey.com reports St. Louis has paired him with David Jiricek.

How much of it lasts? The playmaking looks real: the Blues get about 53% of expected goals at five on five with him out there. The goals look less sturdy: four on 1.9 expected, shooting nearly 13%, and his teammates are finishing well above their chances while he's on the ice. None of his points have come on the power play, which makes the five-on-five production more impressive.

The weak spot from Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking last season was breakouts: only 30% of his exits kept possession. Watch how he handles a heavy forecheck.
headline: Barron has found a home in St. Louis
